# 2018-2022 Completion of College Rate

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)  # For descriptive statistics
library(ggrepel)  # For non-overlapping labels

# Read the dataset
data <- read.csv("../Dataset/v2_2023_gbif_ny.csv")

# Filter the data
data_filtered <- subset(data, Sum_Percent_Land_Use_Agricultural > 0.05)

education_levels <- data_filtered$X2018.2022.Completion.of.College.Rate

# Calculate the complement of Percent_Agricultural_Land_Greater_Than_1km_GBIF
data_filtered <- data_filtered %>%
  mutate(Observational_Coverage = 1 - Percent_Agricultural_Land_Greater_Than_1km_GBIF)

# Define the list of counties to label
counties_to_label <- c("Suffolk", "Tompkins", "Dutchess", "Niagara", 
                        "Ulster", "Clinton", "Allegany", "Lewis", 
                        "Franklin", "Steuben")

# Ensure the correct column name for counties
county_column_name <- "COUNTYNAME"  # Update this if your dataset uses a different column name

# Filter the dataset for only those counties
data_labels <- data_filtered %>% filter(!!sym(county_column_name) %in% counties_to_label)

# Scatterplot with trendline and non-overlapping labels
ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = education_levels, y = Observational_Coverage)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "green") +
  geom_text_repel(data = data_labels, aes(x = X2018.2022.Completion.of.College.Rate, 
                                          y = Observational_Coverage, 
                                          label = !!sym(county_column_name)), 
                  size = 3.5, color = "red", max.overlaps = 10) +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "College Completion Rate (%)",
       y = "Observational Coverage") +
  theme_minimal()

model_edu <- lm(Observational_Coverage ~ education_levels, data = data_filtered)
summary(model_edu)$r.squared  # R²
summary(model_edu)$coefficients[2, 4]  # p-value
summary(model_edu)$coefficients[2, 1]  # slope
```

# 2023 Population Density

2023 Population Density km2

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)  # For descriptive statistics
library(ggrepel)  # For non-overlapping labels

# Read the dataset
data <- read.csv("../Dataset/v2_2023_gbif_ny.csv")

# Filter the data
data_filtered <- subset(data, Sum_Percent_Land_Use_Agricultural > 0.05)

population_density <- data_filtered$X2023.Population.Density.km2

# Calculate the complement of Percent_Agricultural_Land_Greater_Than_1km_GBIF
data_filtered <- data_filtered %>%
  mutate(Observational_Coverage = 1 - Percent_Agricultural_Land_Greater_Than_1km_GBIF)

# Define the list of counties to label
counties_to_label <- c("Suffolk", "Tompkins", "Dutchess", "Niagara", 
                        "Ulster", "Clinton", "Allegany", "Lewis", 
                        "Franklin", "Steuben")

# Ensure the correct column name for counties
county_column_name <- "COUNTYNAME"  # Update this if your dataset uses a different column name

# Filter the dataset for only those counties
data_labels <- data_filtered %>% filter(!!sym(county_column_name) %in% counties_to_label)

# Scatterplot with trendline and non-overlapping labels
ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = population_density, y = Observational_Coverage)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "green") +
  geom_text_repel(data = data_labels, aes(x = X2023.Population.Density.km2, 
                                          y = Observational_Coverage, 
                                          label = !!sym(county_column_name)), 
                  size = 3.5, color = "red", max.overlaps = 10) +
  scale_x_log10() +  # << Log transform axis
  labs(title = "",
       x = "Population Density (People/km², log scale)",
       y = "Observational Coverage") +
  theme_minimal()

data_filtered <- data_filtered %>%
  mutate(log_pop_density = log10(X2023.Population.Density.km2 + 1))

model_density <- lm(Observational_Coverage ~ log_pop_density, data = data_filtered)
summary(model_density)$r.squared
summary(model_density)$coefficients[2, 4]
summary(model_density)$coefficients[2, 1]
```
